posts.headline: Week 9: Pacific Pigskins vs Wascawy Wabbits Headlines a Loaded Slate
posts.body: Week 9 has a rivalry that matters, a 10-1 juggernaut on a six-game heater, and a Maverick squad that's 0-11 and desperate. Here are my picks and the NFL games you need on your screen.
content: Boom! Game of the Week is Pacific Pigskins vs Wascawy Wabbits, and I'm told this one has real bite. The Wascawy Wabbits lead the all-time series 11-5 and have won the last three meetings, including that 171.97-83.42 demolition back in 2018. Their projected 147.4 against 111.0 is a heavy edge, so I'm taking the Wabbits, though Jared Goff gives the Pigskins a real shot. Want to watch every point as it lands? the live scoreboard is where you'll be glued Sunday.

League sources tell me Vitside Mafia are the team to beat at 10-1 and riding a six-game win streak. Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford project to carry them past Running down the Dream, and I'm not betting against that machine. Dark Magicians of Chaos are sinking fast with four straight losses and project 133.2 against Computer Jocks at 132.7, so this is a coin flip I'm calling for the Jocks on Drake Maye's upside. If you think your own depth chart is ready for the grind, double-check your lineup before kickoff.

Bring The Pain are 2-9, riding a six-game losing streak, and I'm told it's getting ugly in that locker room. Gridiron Geeks at 9-2 should handle them, and I'm not losing sleep over that pick. Maverick at 0-11 with an 11-game skid is the worst story in the league, and Music City Mafia are the easy call to snap a little bit of the misery. Check the standings to see just how far the bottom has fallen, and browse the standings while you're there.

Broadcast guide time: Josh Allen and the Bills on the NFL slate is must-see for Vitside Mafia, and Jared Goff's Lions game matters for the Pacific Pigskins. Both teams have a lot riding on their starters clicking in prime time. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs are huge swing players in Detroit's games, so keep an eye on those. Money is nice, but championships are better, so track every one of these games on the live scoreboard and never miss a score.

posts.headline: Week 9 Weekend Preview: Eight Games, Huge Stakes
posts.body: Eight matchups, one doubleheader-free slate, and plenty of teams fighting for their season. I'm told the owners are already sweating their projections. Here's what to watch this weekend.
content: Boom! Week 9 is here, and I'm told the owners are already glued to their screens. Eight matchups on the board, and the stakes are massive. Get your your lineup locked in before kickoff, because this weekend is going to be a battle.

The matchup of the week is Vitside Mafia (10-1) versus Running down the Dream (8-3). Vitside Mafia is projected for 168.8 points, led by Josh Allen at 31.2 and Matthew Stafford at 28.5. Running down the Dream counters with Brock Purdy at 26.7 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 21.8, but league sources tell me that projection gap is tough to overcome. Money is nice, but championships are better, and Vitside Mafia is playing for both.

Pacific Pigskins (9-2) face Wascawy Wabbits (8-3), and this one is loaded. Wascawy Wabbits project at 147.9 with Trevor Lawrence at 26.3 and Jonathan Taylor at 19.0, while Pacific Pigskins lean on Jared Goff at 26.2. Bold prediction: Wascawy Wabbits win this one going away. Track every snap on the live scoreboard and see if I'm right.

Now the teams that need a win. Fire Ready Aim are riding a four-game losing streak and face Da Dangsters (8-3) with Geno Smith, Trey McBride and Chuba Hubbard leading a 125.2-point projection. Dark Magicians of Chaos are also on L4, and Bring The Pain are on a six-game skid, projected at just 104.5 against Gridiron Geeks. Maverick, sitting at 0-11 on an 11-game losing streak, face Music City Mafia, and nobody in the building is calling that one a sure thing. Bold prediction: at least one of these four streaking teams snaps their skid this weekend.

posts.headline: Week 8 Waiver Wire: Minshew Mania, Milton Money
posts.body: Five claims, $3.750M in play, and one bold $1.150M bid for Gardner Minshew. League sources tell me Bring The Pain went all-in on the waiver wire this week, and the rest of the league took notes.
content: Boom! Bring The Pain came out swinging this week, dropping a league-high $1.150M on QB Gardner Minshew. That is the highest single bid of Week 8, and I'm told the front office views it as a stake in the ground, not a flier. Money is nice, but championships are better, and this owner clearly believes Minshew can help them get there.

Gridiron Geeks made the second-biggest splash, paying $1M for WR Courtland Sutton. Sutton is a receiver with real upside, and a million bucks says the Geeks were not interested in waiting around for the next wave. That is an aggressive move in a week where the rest of the league was far more measured.

Music City Mafia went with QB Joe Milton at $750K, a middle-of-the-road bid that says patience over panic. Meanwhile, Wascawy Wabbits and The Mariachi Ninjas both added QBs at the league-minimum $425K through first-come-first-served free-agent pickups. Make no mistake: that $425K is the cost of entry, and no pickup in this league is free. Still, those are the quiet, efficient moves that often end up mattering more than the headline bids.

Five claims, $3.750M spent, and the quarterbacks dominated the board. If you are hunting for the next weekly starter, the free agent board is where those decisions get made, and I'm told it is picking up traffic fast. Check the rosters to see where your depth actually stands before the next waiver run, and set a custom board in your custom rankings board so you are not scrambling when the claims drop.
